laws.rule: Under Paul Miller's Law (75 Pa.C.S. 3316.1, in force 5 June 2025), drivers may not hold a phone or other interactive mobile device in a hand or against the body, dial or answer by pressing more than one button, or reach for it so they leave a normal seated position. This applies while moving and while stopped in traffic or at lights; it doesn't apply once the vehicle has pulled safely off the road. Only written warnings were given for the first 12 months, so fines apply from June 2026. Texting while moving is separately banned (75 Pa.C.S. 3316). Calling police or emergency services to prevent injury is allowed.
laws.penalty_signal: US$50 fine (about A$71 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040).

laws.rule: Pennsylvania State Police guidance: anyone over 18 can buy, possess and use consumer fireworks, and must buy them from a licensed stand-alone permanent store (online orders must be collected at a licensed facility). They may not be set off on property without permission, pointed at a building or vehicle, used within 150 feet of any building or vehicle (even your own) or used while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Municipalities may restrict use between 10 pm and 10 am, except until 1 am on 2, 3 and 4 July and 31 December. Ground and hand-held sparkling devices, novelties and toy caps aren't counted as consumer fireworks and are allowed at all times.

items.text: Pennsylvania's Medical Marijuana Program is open to Pennsylvanians who have one or more of 24 qualifying serious medical conditions and a certification from an approved practitioner. The Department of Health's program page says nothing about accepting medical cards from other states.
Wine and spirits are sold by the state: the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board runs about 560 Fine Wine & Good Spirits stores statewide, and licenses the state's other alcohol producers and sellers.
